alt: Table listing, for each derivation in Appendix B, the claim, the numerical check run in the build script, the result, and whether it is consistent with the claim.
note: Consistent means the check behaved as the derivation says under its conditions; a check is not a proof.

rows.check: Poisson sampling, 20,000 draws, outcome unrelated to pi
rows.claim: HT total is design-unbiased when every pi_i > 0 and is known
rows.result: HT mean minus T = -0.88 Monte Carlo SEs

rows.check: same draws, outcome unrelated to pi
rows.claim: Hajek mean is not exactly unbiased; its variance can be far below HT/N's

rows.check: Poisson sampling, 20,000 draws, outcome proportional to pi
rows.claim: HT total is design-unbiased when every pi_i > 0 and is known
rows.result: HT mean minus T = -0.82 Monte Carlo SEs

rows.check: same draws, outcome proportional to pi
rows.claim: Hajek mean is not exactly unbiased; its variance can be far below HT/N's

rows.check: hand formula vs svy vs pyfixest CRV1, 40 PSUs
rows.claim: One stratum, weighted mean: Taylor (with replacement) equals CRV1 exactly
rows.result: svy vs hand 0.0e+00; CRV1 vs svy 0.0e+00 (relative)

rows.claim: Informative strata: CRV1 omits the stratification gain and is conservative
rows.result: CRV1 SE / Taylor SE = 2.22; with uninformative strata 0.98

rows.check: slope SE: svy GLM vs hand sandwich vs pyfixest CRV1
rows.claim: Regression (K = 2): CRV1 = Taylor x (N - 1)/(N - K), a small-sample factor
rows.result: svy vs hand 1.3e-16; CRV1 / svy = 1.000748 vs sqrt((N-1)/(N-K)) = 1.000748

rows.check: equal clusters (m = 20), rho_u = 0.1, regressor constant within clusters
rows.claim: Moulton: Var(OLS slope) / conventional OLS variance = 1 + (m - 1) rho_x rho_u

rows.check: equal clusters (m = 20), rho_u = 0.1, regressor half within-cluster
rows.claim: Moulton: Var(OLS slope) / conventional OLS variance = 1 + (m - 1) rho_x rho_u
